config.description: v031's exact recipe with a BETTER TEACHER. Student unchanged: hidden 128, input_proj 64, distill_weight 2.0, 3 epochs, same architecture and seed. Only the distillation targets change.
config.hypothesis:
The teacher's quality is the one input to distillation we have never varied, and a strictly better one is on disk. Our current teacher is dozken's reset2k at 0.6864 local. His two-graph loss-diverse ensemble of reset2k + reset4k is 0.6879, which is 0.0015 better, and it is free at inference because a teacher never runs at serving time.

  TeacherStore already averages multiple label files on read, so pointing loss.teacher_labels at both members reproduces his raw-mean ensemble exactly with no change to the training script. His solution.py confirms the average is raw (scale = 1/len(graphs), no z-scoring), which matters because the metric clips at +/-2.

  The honest prior is POOR and stated as such. dozken's distil_ens scored 0.6585 against his distil160's 0.6588, so on his pair a better teacher did not beat a worse one through compression. The visible reason is that his student already sat at the compression sweet spot, leaving no gap for the teacher's extra 0.0015 to close.

  Our student is somewhere different: 225,922 params at 0.687376 against a 0.6864 teacher, so it has ALREADY OVERTAKEN the single-model teacher. That is new -- none of dozken's students beat their own teacher locally. Whether that means there is headroom for a better teacher, or that the student has extracted everything extractable, is exactly the question. Worth one run, not worth assuming.
config.change_vs_parent: loss.teacher_labels gains a second member so TeacherStore averages dozken's reset2k and reset4k into his 0.6879 ensemble. Student architecture, distill_weight, schedule and seed all unchanged.
